specs.instructions: Convert accepted input units to barg and round to one decimal after conversion. A pressure unit without a gauge or absolute indication is read as gauge.
specs.flag_when: If conversion would require changing gauge pressure to absolute pressure or absolute pressure to gauge pressure, leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.rules:
7.4 Gauge pressure shall be held in barg. The following are accepted for gauge pressure: ‘barg’, ‘bar g’, ‘bar(g)’ and ‘bar’ without conversion; ‘psig’, ‘psi’ and ‘psi(g)’, to be multiplied by 0.0689476; ‘kPa’ and ‘kPag’, to be multiplied by 0.01; ‘MPa’ and ‘MPag’, to be multiplied by 10; and ‘kg/cm2’, to be multiplied by 0.980665. A pressure unit received without a gauge or absolute indication in a gauge attribute shall be read as gauge. Gauge pressure is rounded to one decimal after conversion.
7.7 Gauge pressure shall not be converted to absolute pressure, and absolute pressure shall not be converted to gauge pressure.
17.1 Pressure vessels hold Orientation, Inside diameter, Length, Design pressure, Design temperature, Material, Head type, Design code, Radiography and PWHT. Inside diameter and Length, the latter measured tangent to tangent, are short lengths in mm. Design pressure is a gauge pressure in barg. PWHT is Yes or No.
17.4 Shell-and-tube heat exchangers hold TEMA type, Duty, Area, Shell design pressure, Tube design pressure and Tube material. Duty is held in kW, Area in m2, and both design pressures in barg.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted input units to bara and round to one decimal after conversion.
specs.flag_when: If the pressure unit does not contain an absolute indication, or if conversion would require changing gauge pressure to absolute pressure or absolute pressure to gauge pressure, leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.rules:
7.5 Absolute pressure shall be held in bara. The following are accepted for absolute pressure: ‘bara’, ‘bar a’ and ‘bar(a)’ without conversion, and ‘psia’, to be multiplied by 0.0689476. A pressure unit received without an absolute indication in an absolute attribute is not accepted and the value shall be entered in the query register. Absolute pressure is rounded to one decimal after conversion.
7.7 Gauge pressure shall not be converted to absolute pressure, and absolute pressure shall not be converted to gauge pressure.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted input units to bar and round to two decimals after conversion.
specs.rules: 7.6 Differential pressure shall be held in bar. The following are accepted for differential pressure: ‘bar’ without conversion; ‘mbar’, to be multiplied by 0.001; ‘psi’ and ‘psid’, to be multiplied by 0.0689476; and ‘kPa’, to be multiplied by 0.01. Differential pressure is rounded to two decimals after conversion.

specs.instructions: Convert Fahrenheit by reducing it by 32, multiplying by 5/9, and rounding to a whole number. Write a result of minus zero as 0.
specs.rules:
7.8 Temperature shall be held in degC. The spellings ‘degC’, ‘deg C’, ‘°C’, and a letter ‘C’ standing alone after the number, are accepted without conversion. A temperature received in degrees Fahrenheit, written ‘degF’, ‘deg F’, ‘°F’ or as a letter ‘F’ standing alone after the number, shall be reduced by 32, multiplied by 5/9 and rounded to a whole number. A result of minus zero shall be written as 0.
17.1 Pressure vessels hold Orientation, Inside diameter, Length, Design pressure, Design temperature, Material, Head type, Design code, Radiography and PWHT. Inside diameter and Length, the latter measured tangent to tangent, are short lengths in mm. Design pressure is a gauge pressure in barg. PWHT is Yes or No.
17.3 Storage tanks hold Capacity, Diameter, Height, Roof, Design code and Design temperature. Capacity is held in m3; Diameter and Height are long lengths in m.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted short-length units to mm and round to one decimal after conversion. Do not convert an outside diameter to an inside diameter.
specs.rules:
3.11 Short length: a dimension of a component or instrument, including diameters, thicknesses, insertion lengths and stud lengths.
7.9 Short lengths shall be held in mm. The following are accepted: ‘mm’ without conversion; inches, written with an inch mark or as ‘in’, ‘inch’ or ‘inches’, to be multiplied by 25.4; ‘cm’, to be multiplied by 10; and ‘m’, to be multiplied by 1000. Short lengths are rounded to one decimal after conversion.
7.10 Long lengths shall be held in m. The following are accepted: ‘m’, ‘mtr’, ‘meter’, ‘meters’, ‘metre’ and ‘metres’ without conversion; ‘mm’, to be multiplied by 0.001; and feet, written ‘ft’ or ‘feet’ or with an apostrophe, to be multiplied by 0.3048. Long lengths are rounded to two decimals after conversion. Clauses 12 to 18 identify the attributes held as long lengths; every other length attribute is a short length.
17.1 Pressure vessels hold Orientation, Inside diameter, Length, Design pressure, Design temperature, Material, Head type, Design code, Radiography and PWHT. Inside diameter and Length, the latter measured tangent to tangent, are short lengths in mm. Design pressure is a gauge pressure in barg. PWHT is Yes or No.
17.2 An outside diameter shall not be converted to an inside diameter.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted long-length units to m and round to two decimals after conversion.
specs.rules:
3.12 Long length: a length of cable or pipe, the height or diameter of a storage tank, pump head and similar dimensions of large magnitude.
7.10 Long lengths shall be held in m. The following are accepted: ‘m’, ‘mtr’, ‘meter’, ‘meters’, ‘metre’ and ‘metres’ without conversion; ‘mm’, to be multiplied by 0.001; and feet, written ‘ft’ or ‘feet’ or with an apostrophe, to be multiplied by 0.3048. Long lengths are rounded to two decimals after conversion. Clauses 12 to 18 identify the attributes held as long lengths; every other length attribute is a short length.
17.3 Storage tanks hold Capacity, Diameter, Height, Roof, Design code and Design temperature. Capacity is held in m3; Diameter and Height are long lengths in m.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted input units to m3/h, then round the result to one decimal place. Write the number followed by one space and m3/h; trailing zeros are removed.
specs.flag_when: If the required unit is missing, the input contains an unresolved qualifier or ambiguity, or it cannot be presented unambiguously, leave it unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.rules: 7.11 Volumetric flow shall be held in m3/h. The following are accepted: ‘m3/h’, ‘m3/hr’, ‘m3/h’ and ‘cmh’ without conversion; US gallons per minute, written ‘gpm’ or ‘USgpm’, to be multiplied by 0.2271; litres per second, written ‘l/s’, to be multiplied by 3.6; and litres per minute, written ‘l/min’, to be multiplied by 0.06. Flow is rounded to one decimal after conversion.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted input units to kW, then round the result to one decimal place. Write the number followed by one space and kW; trailing zeros are removed.
specs.flag_when: If the required unit is missing, the input contains an unresolved qualifier or ambiguity, or it cannot be presented unambiguously, leave it unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.rules:
7.12 Power, including heat duty, shall be held in kW. The following are accepted: ‘kW’ without conversion; ‘hp’ and ‘bhp’, to be multiplied by 0.746; ‘W’, to be multiplied by 0.001; and ‘MW’, to be multiplied by 1000. Power is rounded to one decimal after conversion.
17.4 Shell-and-tube heat exchangers hold TEMA type, Duty, Area, Shell design pressure, Tube design pressure and Tube material. Duty is held in kW, Area in m2, and both design pressures in barg.

specs.instructions: Convert MVA to kVA, then round the result to one decimal place. Write the number followed by one space and kVA; trailing zeros are removed.
specs.flag_when: If the required unit is missing, the input contains an unresolved qualifier or ambiguity, or it cannot be presented unambiguously, leave it unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.rules: 7.13 Apparent power, used for transformers and UPS systems, shall be held in kVA. ‘kVA’ is accepted without conversion and ‘MVA’ is to be multiplied by 1000. Apparent power is rounded to one decimal after conversion.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted input units to kg, then round the result to one decimal place. Write the number followed by one space and kg; trailing zeros are removed.
specs.flag_when: If the required unit is missing, the input contains an unresolved qualifier or ambiguity, or it cannot be presented unambiguously, leave it unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.rules: 7.14 Mass shall be held in kg. The following are accepted: ‘kg’ and ‘kgs’ without conversion; pounds, written ‘lb’ or ‘lbs’, to be multiplied by 0.4536; and tonnes, written ‘t’, to be multiplied by 1000. Mass is rounded to one decimal after conversion.

specs.instructions: For vessels and tanks, convert accepted input units to m3, then round the result to one decimal place. Write the number followed by one space and m3; trailing zeros are removed.
specs.flag_when: If the required unit is missing, a non-permitted unit is used for an extinguisher charge, the input contains an unresolved qualifier or ambiguity, or it cannot be presented unambiguously, leave it unchanged and enter it in the query register.

variants.applies_to: the charge of foam and water extinguishers
variants.instructions: Hold the charge in l and round it to one decimal place. Write the number followed by one space and l; no other unit is accepted and trailing zeros are removed.
variants.flag_when: If the unit is not l, the input contains an unresolved qualifier or ambiguity, or it cannot be presented unambiguously, leave it unchanged and enter it in the query register.

specs.rules:
7.15 The volume of vessels and tanks shall be held in m3. The following are accepted: ‘m3’ and ‘m3’ without conversion; litres, written ‘l’ or ‘ltr’, to be multiplied by 0.001; and barrels, written ‘bbl’, to be multiplied by 0.159. Volume is rounded to one decimal after conversion. The charge of foam and water extinguishers is held in l, and no other unit is accepted for it.
17.3 Storage tanks hold Capacity, Diameter, Height, Roof, Design code and Design temperature. Capacity is held in m3; Diameter and Height are long lengths in m.

specs.instructions: Convert accepted input units to m2, then round the result to one decimal place. Write the number followed by one space and m2; trailing zeros are removed.
specs.flag_when: If the required unit is missing, the input contains an unresolved qualifier or ambiguity, or it cannot be presented unambiguously, leave it unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.rules:
7.16 Area shall be held in m2. The following are accepted: ‘m2’, ‘m2’ and ‘sq m’ without conversion, and square feet, written ‘sq ft’ or ‘ft2’, to be multiplied by 0.0929. Area is rounded to one decimal after conversion.
17.4 Shell-and-tube heat exchangers hold TEMA type, Duty, Area, Shell design pressure, Tube design pressure and Tube material. Duty is held in kW, Area in m2, and both design pressures in barg.

specs.instructions: Write rotational speed in rpm. Accept rpm, RPM, r/min and min-1 without conversion.
specs.rules: 7.17 Rotational speed shall be held in rpm, and ‘rpm’, ‘RPM’, ‘r/min’ and ‘min-1’ are accepted without conversion. Frequency shall be held in Hz. Current shall be held in A, ‘kA’ being accepted and multiplied by 1000. Durations such as battery autonomy shall be held in min, hours written ‘h’ or ‘hr’ being multiplied by 60 and rounded to a whole number.

specs.instructions: Write frequency in Hz.
specs.rules: 7.17 Rotational speed shall be held in rpm, and ‘rpm’, ‘RPM’, ‘r/min’ and ‘min-1’ are accepted without conversion. Frequency shall be held in Hz. Current shall be held in A, ‘kA’ being accepted and multiplied by 1000. Durations such as battery autonomy shall be held in min, hours written ‘h’ or ‘hr’ being multiplied by 60 and rounded to a whole number.

specs.instructions: Write current in A. Convert an input in kA by multiplying by 1000.
specs.rules: 7.17 Rotational speed shall be held in rpm, and ‘rpm’, ‘RPM’, ‘r/min’ and ‘min-1’ are accepted without conversion. Frequency shall be held in Hz. Current shall be held in A, ‘kA’ being accepted and multiplied by 1000. Durations such as battery autonomy shall be held in min, hours written ‘h’ or ‘hr’ being multiplied by 60 and rounded to a whole number.

specs.instructions: Write duration in min. Convert hours written as h or hr by multiplying by 60 and round to a whole number.
specs.rules: 7.17 Rotational speed shall be held in rpm, and ‘rpm’, ‘RPM’, ‘r/min’ and ‘min-1’ are accepted without conversion. Frequency shall be held in Hz. Current shall be held in A, ‘kA’ being accepted and multiplied by 1000. Durations such as battery autonomy shall be held in min, hours written ‘h’ or ‘hr’ being multiplied by 60 and rounded to a whole number.

specs.instructions: Write the nominal size as NPS, a space and the size, without an inch mark. Write fractional sizes with a hyphen between the whole number and the fraction; convert the listed DN sizes to their specified NPS sizes.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register when a number followed by mm alone is received, or when the DN or NPS size is not listed.
specs.rules:
8.1 The nominal size of pipe, valves, fittings and flanges shall be expressed in inches in the form NPS, a space and the size, without an inch mark. A fractional size shall be written with a hyphen between the whole number and the fraction.
8.2 The following received forms are recognized as nominal sizes in inches: the size followed by an inch mark or by ‘in’, ‘inch’ or ‘inches’; the size preceded by ‘NPS’, with or without an intervening space; and an inch size followed by ‘NB’, the NB being disregarded. A fraction separated from the whole number by a space, a fraction written with a Unicode fraction character and a decimal size shall each be rewritten as the hyphenated fraction.
8.3 A size in DN shall be converted to NPS as follows: DN15 to NPS 1/2; DN20 to NPS 3/4; DN25 to NPS 1; DN32 to NPS 1-1/4; DN40 to NPS 1-1/2; DN50 to NPS 2; DN65 to NPS 2-1/2; DN80 to NPS 3; DN100 to NPS 4; DN150 to NPS 6; DN200 to NPS 8; DN250 to NPS 10; DN300 to NPS 12; DN350 to NPS 14; DN400 to NPS 16; DN450 to NPS 18; DN500 to NPS 20; and DN600 to NPS 24.
8.4 A DN size is recognized where the letters DN precede or follow the number, with or without a space, and where the number is followed by ‘NB’ or ‘mm NB’. A number followed by mm alone is not recognized as a nominal size, since it is frequently an outside diameter, and shall be entered in the query register. A DN or NPS not listed in 8.3 shall likewise be entered in the query register.

specs.instructions: Write the pressure class as CL, a space and the class number. Recognize Class, CL or ANSI before the number, a hash sign before or after the number, lb or lbs after the number, and class after the number.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register when the class number is not 150, 300, 600, 800, 900, 1500 or 2500; do not convert a PN rating to a pressure class.
specs.rules:
8.5 A pressure class shall be written as CL, a space and the class number. The class numbers in use are 150, 300, 600, 800, 900, 1500 and 2500, and any other number shall be entered in the query register. The received forms recognized are ‘Class’, ‘CL’ or ‘ANSI’ preceding the number, with or without a space; a hash sign preceding or following the number; ‘lb’ or ‘lbs’ following the number; and ‘class’ following the number.
8.7 A pressure class shall not be converted to a PN rating and a PN rating shall not be converted to a pressure class. The attribute Rating may hold either.

specs.instructions: Write the value as PN, a space, and one of 6, 10, 16, 25, 40, 63, or 100. Recognize PN before or after the number, separated by a space, hyphen, or nothing, and do not convert a pressure class to a PN rating.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if it is not an unambiguous PN rating.
specs.rules:
8.6 A PN rating shall be written as PN, a space and the number. The PN numbers in use are 6, 10, 16, 25, 40, 63 and 100. The letters PN may precede or follow the number in the received value, separated from it by a space, by a hyphen or by nothing.
8.7 A pressure class shall not be converted to a PN rating and a PN rating shall not be converted to a pressure class. The attribute Rating may hold either.

specs.instructions: Write a numbered schedule as SCH, a space, and the schedule; retain S immediately after the number for a stainless steel schedule. Write weight designations as SCH STD, SCH XS, or SCH XXS, recognizing standard, standard weight, extra strong, and double extra strong as specified.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the schedule cannot be presented unambiguously.
specs.rules: 8.8 A pipe schedule shall be written as SCH, a space and the schedule. ‘Sch’, ‘SCH’, ‘Schedule’ and ‘S-’ preceding the schedule are recognized, with or without a space or full stop. The weight designations are written SCH STD, SCH XS and SCH XXS; the received words ‘standard’, ‘standard weight’ and ‘STD’ denote SCH STD, ‘extra strong’ and ‘XS’ denote SCH XS, and ‘double extra strong’ and ‘XXS’ denote SCH XXS. A schedule number followed by the letter S is a stainless steel schedule distinct from the same number without the letter, and the S shall be retained immediately after the number.

specs.instructions: Write the size in inches as a fraction followed immediately by an inch mark, then a space and NPT; when known, write FNPT or MNPT immediately before NPT. Recognize the stated gender forms and rewrite the stated decimal sizes as the specified fractions.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the size or gender is ambiguous.
specs.rules:
8.9 A taper pipe thread shall be written as the size in inches as a fraction, followed without a space by an inch mark, then a space and NPT. Where the gender is known it shall be written immediately before NPT without a space, giving FNPT for female threads and MNPT for male threads.
8.10 The gender of a taper pipe thread is recognized from ‘F’, ‘female’, ‘FNPT’, ‘NPTF’, ‘NPT(F)’ and ‘NPT-F’, and correspondingly from ‘M’, ‘male’, ‘MNPT’, ‘NPTM’, ‘NPT(M)’ and ‘NPT-M’, in any position relative to NPT. The size may be received with an inch mark, ‘in’ or ‘inch’, or as a Unicode fraction character; a decimal size shall be rewritten as a fraction, 0.25 becoming 1/4, 0.5 becoming 1/2, 0.75 becoming 3/4, 1.5 becoming 1-1/2, and 1 and 2 remaining as whole numbers.

specs.instructions: Write M immediately followed by the diameter and, only when received, a lower case x followed by the pitch, with no spaces. Recognize spaces and an upper case X in the received value.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the received value does not unambiguously identify the metric thread.
specs.rules: 8.11 A metric thread shall be written as M followed without a space by the diameter and, where the pitch is received, a lower case x and the pitch, likewise without spaces. A pitch shall be neither added where it was not received nor deleted where it was. Spaces and an upper case X in the received value are recognized.

specs.instructions: Write an inch-series diameter as the specified fraction followed immediately by an inch mark, rewriting the specified decimal diameters as fractions. Write metric bolt diameters in accordance with the metric thread form, and do not convert inch and metric diameters into one another.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the diameter system or value is ambiguous.
specs.rules: 8.12 The diameter of an inch-series bolt or stud shall be written as the fraction followed without a space by an inch mark. The fraction followed by ‘in’, ‘inch’ or an inch mark is recognized, and decimal diameters shall be rewritten as fractions: 0.5 as 1/2, 0.625 as 5/8, 0.75 as 3/4, 0.875 as 7/8, 1.125 as 1-1/8 and 1.25 as 1-1/4, with 1 remaining as a whole number. Metric bolt diameters are written in accordance with 8.11. Inch and metric bolt diameters shall not be converted into one another.

specs.instructions: For a voltage below 1000 V, write the number, a space, and VAC or VDC; for 1000 V or more, write the number, a space, and kV. Rewrite received kV values below 1 kV in V and received V values of 1000 or more in kV, and recognize the stated AC and DC forms.
specs.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register when neither the equipment clause nor the received value states whether the voltage is AC or DC.

variants.instructions: Write the voltage as an AC voltage, adding VAC when it is not received; write 1000 V and above in kV in accordance with the general voltage rule.
variants.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the voltage cannot be presented unambiguously.

variants.applies_to: a three-phase voltage stated together with its phase voltage
variants.instructions: Write the two numbers separated by a slash without spaces, with the higher first, followed by a space and VAC.
variants.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the two voltage values or their order is ambiguous.

variants.instructions: Write the rated voltage as Uo and U in kV, separated by a slash without spaces, followed by a space and kV. Rewrite values received in V in kV and delete Uo/U when it precedes the numbers.
variants.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the cable voltage rating cannot be presented unambiguously.

variants.instructions: Write the voltage ratio as the two voltages in kV, separated by a slash without spaces, with the high voltage first.
variants.flag_when: Leave the value unchanged and enter it in the query register if the transformer voltage ratio or its order is ambiguous.

specs.rules:
9.1 A voltage below 1000 V shall be written as the number, a space and VAC or VDC. A voltage of 1000 V or more shall be written in kV as the number, a space and kV, with no suffix, all high voltage in the installations covered being alternating current.
9.2 A received voltage expressed in kV but below 1 kV shall be rewritten in V, and a received voltage expressed in V and equal to or greater than 1000 shall be rewritten in kV.
9.3 Alternating current is recognized from ‘V AC’, ‘VAC’ and ‘Vac’ following the number and from ‘AC’ preceding it; direct current is recognized from ‘V DC’, ‘VDC’ and ‘Vdc’ following the number and from ‘DC’ preceding it. Where Clauses 12 to 18 state that an attribute is AC or DC and the received value does not state it, VAC or VDC as appropriate shall be added. Where neither the equipment clause nor the received value states it, the value shall be entered in the query register.
9.4 A three-phase voltage stated together with its phase voltage shall be written as the two numbers separated by a slash without spaces, the higher first, followed by a space and VAC.
9.5 The rated voltage of a cable shall be written as Uo and U in kV, separated by a slash without spaces, followed by a space and kV. Values received in V shall be rewritten in kV, and the characters ‘Uo/U’ preceding the numbers shall be deleted. The voltage ratio of a transformer shall be written in the same manner with the high voltage first, both voltages in kV.
14.3 Electric motors hold Power, Voltage, Frequency, Speed, Efficiency class, Insulation class, IP rating, Ex marking and Mounting. Power is held in kW. Voltage is an AC attribute: VAC shall be added where it is not received, and 1000 V and above are written in kV in accordance with 9.1.
16.1 Power, control and instrument cables hold Voltage rating, Size, Insulation, Armour, Sheath, Screen and Length. Size is a cable size in accordance with 9.17 and 9.18. Length is a long length in m.

specs.instructions: Write the signal using the prescribed form and exactly the prescribed capitals. Leave any other signal unchanged and enter it in the query register.
specs.flag_when: Any other signal shall be left unchanged and entered in the query register.
specs.rules:
9.6 An analogue signal shall be written 4-20mA without any space, and with HART as 4-20mA HART, a single space preceding HART. The received forms ‘4-20 mA’, ‘4..20mA’, ‘4…20 mA’, ‘4 to 20 mA’ and ‘4~20mA’ are recognized, as are the same forms followed by HART and the forms ‘4-20 mA + HART’, ‘4-20mA/HART’ and ‘HART 4-20mA’.
9.7 Foundation Fieldbus shall be written in that form, ‘FF’, ‘FF H1’ and ‘FOUNDATION fieldbus’ being recognized. Profibus PA shall be written in that form, ‘PROFIBUS-PA’ and ‘PB-PA’ being recognized. A volt-free contact shall be written Volt-free contact, ‘VFC’, ‘dry contact’ and ‘potential-free contact’ being recognized. Any other signal shall be entered in the query register.
12.5 Control valves hold Size, Rating, Body material, Cv, Characteristic, Leakage class, Actuator, Fail position and Positioner signal. Actuator uses the terms of Operator, but only Pneumatic actuator and Electric actuator are admissible for control valves, and any other value shall be entered in the query register. Positioner signal is a signal in accordance with Clause 9. A Kv value shall not be converted to Cv.
15.1 Pressure transmitters hold Range, Output, Accuracy, Process connection, Wetted material, IP rating, Ex marking and Power supply. Range is a range of gauge pressure in barg and is the calibrated range. Output is a signal in accordance with Clause 9. Process connection is a taper pipe thread. Power supply is a DC attribute, and VDC shall be added where it is not received.
18.1 Gas detectors hold Principle, Gas, Range, Output and Ex marking. Range is held in %LEL for flammable gases, in ppm for toxic gases and in %vol for oxygen.

specs.instructions: Write an IP code as IP followed directly by its two digits. For a dual rating, write the first complete code, a slash, and the two digits of the second code only.
specs.rules:
9.8 An IP code shall be written as IP followed directly by its two digits. Spaces and hyphens between IP and the digits in the received value are recognized. A dual rating shall be written as the first complete code, a slash and the two digits of the second code only; the received value may carry IP before both codes or before the first only.
14.3 Electric motors hold Power, Voltage, Frequency, Speed, Efficiency class, Insulation class, IP rating, Ex marking and Mounting. Power is held in kW. Voltage is an AC attribute: VAC shall be added where it is not received, and 1000 V and above are written in kV in accordance with 9.1.
15.1 Pressure transmitters hold Range, Output, Accuracy, Process connection, Wetted material, IP rating, Ex marking and Power supply. Range is a range of gauge pressure in barg and is the calibrated range. Output is a signal in accordance with Clause 9. Process connection is a taper pipe thread. Power supply is a DC attribute, and VDC shall be added where it is not received.
16.3 Cable glands hold Gland type, Thread, Material, Ex marking and IP rating. Thread is a metric thread or a taper pipe thread in accordance with Clause 8, and a metric thread shall not be converted to an NPT size.
16.4 Junction boxes hold Material, Dimensions, Terminals, Entries, IP rating and Ex marking. Dimensions are width, height and depth in mm in that order, written in accordance with 6.13. Terminals and Entries are counts in accordance with 11.25.
B.2 Registers prepared before this edition may contain dual IP codes written in an earlier form. Such values are presented in accordance with 9.8 in the same manner as any other received value.

specs.instructions: Write Ex followed by the protection code or codes, gas group, temperature class and, where received, equipment protection level, in that order with single spaces. Write protection codes in lower case except n-type codes, gas groups as IIA, IIB or IIC, temperature classes as T followed by a digit, and equipment protection levels as G followed by a lower-case letter; write EEx as Ex and do not add unreceived elements.
specs.flag_when: Markings for dust, ATEX category markings and certificate numbers, and values containing them, shall be left unchanged and entered in the query register.
specs.rules:
9.9 An Ex marking shall be written as Ex followed by the protection code or codes, the gas group, the temperature class and, where received, the equipment protection level, in that sequence and separated by single spaces.
9.10 Within an Ex marking, protection codes are written in lower case, with the exception of the n-type codes, which consist of a lower case n followed by an upper case letter. The gas group is written in capitals as IIA, IIB or IIC, and IIB+H2 is written without spaces. The temperature class is an upper case T followed by its digit. The equipment protection level is an upper case G followed by a lower case letter.
9.11 The former prefix EEx shall be written Ex, and Ex received in any capitals is recognized. Hyphens and commas separating the parts of a received marking shall be treated as spaces. No element shall be added that was not received; in particular a level letter shall not be added to a protection code received without one, and an equipment protection level shall not be derived from the other elements. Markings for dust, ATEX category markings and certificate numbers are outside the scope of this standard, and values containing them shall be entered in the query register.
14.3 Electric motors hold Power, Voltage, Frequency, Speed, Efficiency class, Insulation class, IP rating, Ex marking and Mounting. Power is held in kW. Voltage is an AC attribute: VAC shall be added where it is not received, and 1000 V and above are written in kV in accordance with 9.1.
15.1 Pressure transmitters hold Range, Output, Accuracy, Process connection, Wetted material, IP rating, Ex marking and Power supply. Range is a range of gauge pressure in barg and is the calibrated range. Output is a signal in accordance with Clause 9. Process connection is a taper pipe thread. Power supply is a DC attribute, and VDC shall be added where it is not received.
16.3 Cable glands hold Gland type, Thread, Material, Ex marking and IP rating. Thread is a metric thread or a taper pipe thread in accordance with Clause 8, and a metric thread shall not be converted to an NPT size.
16.4 Junction boxes hold Material, Dimensions, Terminals, Entries, IP rating and Ex marking. Dimensions are width, height and depth in mm in that order, written in accordance with 6.13. Terminals and Entries are counts in accordance with 11.25.
18.1 Gas detectors hold Principle, Gas, Range, Output and Ex marking. Range is held in %LEL for flammable gases, in ppm for toxic gases and in %vol for oxygen.

specs.instructions: Write the motor efficiency class as IE followed directly by the digit. Remove spaces and hyphens between IE and the digit.
specs.rules:
9.12 A motor efficiency class shall be written as IE followed directly by the digit; spaces and hyphens between them in the received value are recognized.

variants.instructions: Write the number of pairs, a space, the word pair, a space, a lower case x, a space, the cross-section, a space and mm2. Treat P, pr, pair and pairs as denoting pairs.

specs.rules:
A cable size shall be written as the number of cores, a space, a lower case x, a space, the cross-section, a space and mm2. A paired cable shall be written as the number of pairs, a space, the word pair, a space, a lower case x, a space, the cross-section, a space and mm2, and a triad cable in the same manner using the word triad.
In a received cable size, ‘C’, ‘core’ and ‘cores’ following a number denote cores, ‘P’, ‘pr’, ‘pair’ and ‘pairs’ denote pairs, and ‘T’, ‘triad’ and ‘triads’ denote triads; a number multiplied by a cross-section without any of these words denotes cores. The cross-section unit is recognized from ‘mm2’, ‘mm²’, ‘sq mm’ and ‘sqmm’. A cross-section received without a unit or in AWG shall be entered in the query register.

specs.instructions: Apply the prescribed material designation, removing ASTM, Gr, Gr. and Grade as specified, writing the ASME prefix SA or SA- as A, replacing the specification-grade hyphen with a space, and writing grades in capitals. A grade received without its specification is accepted only where recognized in this clause.
Forged carbon steel is written A105, with ‘ASTM A105’, ‘SA105’, ‘SA-105’ and ‘A-105’ recognized. Seamless carbon steel pipe is written A106 B, with ‘A106 Gr B’, ‘A106 Gr.B’, ‘A106-B’, ‘ASTM A106 Grade B’ and ‘SA106 B’ recognized. Low-temperature pipe is written A333 6, with ‘A333 Gr 6’ recognized.
Cast carbon steel is written A216 WCB, with the grade ‘WCB’ alone and ‘ASTM A216 WCB’, ‘A216 Gr WCB’ and ‘SA216 WCB’ recognized. Low-temperature cast steel is written A352 LCC, with ‘LCC’ recognized. Cast stainless steel is written A351 CF8M, with ‘CF8M’ and ‘ASTM A351 CF8M’ recognized. Forged stainless steel is written A182 F316 or A182 F316L, with ‘F316’, ‘F316L’, ‘ASTM A182 F316’ and ‘ASTM A182 F316L’ recognized.
Carbon steel fittings are written A234 WPB, with ‘WPB’ recognized, and stainless steel fittings A403 WP316L, with ‘WP316L’ recognized. Plate is written A516 70, with ‘A516 Gr 70’, ‘SA-516 70’, ‘SA516 Gr.70’ and ‘ASTM A516 Grade 70’ recognized. Heat exchanger tubes are written A179, with ‘SA179’ recognized.
Stud material is written A193 B7 or A193 B7M, with ‘B7’, ‘ASTM A193 B7’ and ‘A193 Gr B7’ recognized for the former. Nut material is written A194 2H or A194 2HM, with ‘2H’, ‘ASTM A194 2H’ and ‘A194 Gr 2H’ recognized for the former.
10.6 Stainless steel without an ASTM designation is written as SS followed directly by the grade number, namely SS304, SS316 and SS316L. For each grade the forms ‘SS’ followed by a space and the grade, the grade followed by ‘SS’ or ‘SS’, ‘AISI’ followed by the grade, ‘S.S.’ followed by the grade, ‘stainless steel’ followed by the grade and the grade followed by ‘stainless’ are recognized. Stainless steel received without any grade shall not be assigned one; it shall be entered in the query register.
10.7 Carbon steel without a designation is written CS, with ‘carbon steel’ and ‘C.S.’ recognized. Low-temperature carbon steel is written LTCS. Duplex stainless steel is written Duplex SS, with ‘duplex’, ‘duplex stainless steel’ and ‘DSS’ recognized.
10.8 Hot dip galvanized steel is written HDG steel, with ‘hot dip galvanized steel’, ‘hot-dip galvanised steel’ and ‘galvanized steel (HDG)’ recognized. Painted carbon steel is written Painted CS, with ‘painted carbon steel’ and ‘painted steel’ recognized.
10.9 Aluminium is written with the British spelling, Aluminium, with ‘aluminum’ and ‘Al’ recognized. Nickel plated brass is written Ni-plated brass, with ‘nickel plated brass’ and ‘NP brass’ recognized, and brass without plating is written Brass. Glass reinforced plastic is written GRP, with ‘glass reinforced polyester’, ‘FRP’ and ‘fiberglass’ recognized. Ductile iron is written Ductile iron, with ‘DI’ and ‘SG iron’ recognized.
10.10 Copper is written Copper, with ‘Cu’ recognized, and tinned copper is written Tinned copper. Nickel alloy 625 is written Alloy 625, with ‘Inconel 625’ and ‘UNS N06625’ recognized. Stellite hard facing is written Stellite 6, with ‘St6’ recognized.
10.11 Non-metallic materials are written PTFE, with ‘Teflon’ recognized; RPTFE, with ‘reinforced PTFE’ and ‘R-PTFE’ recognized; Graphite, with ‘flexible graphite’ and ‘Grafoil’ recognized; FKM, with ‘Viton’ and ‘FPM’ recognized; NBR, with ‘nitrile’ and ‘Buna-N’ recognized; EPDM; and PEEK.
10.12 Any other material, including trade names not mentioned in this clause and values naming two materials, shall be left unchanged and entered in the query register.
